payload.name: Extract explicit advice as memories
payload.description: When a speaker gives explicit advice, recommendations, or instructions to another person about how to do something, during extraction, create a memory capturing the advice and its topic.
content: During candidate extraction, when a speaker explicitly advises, recommends, or instructs another person on how to do or decide something, create a memory that captures the advice (what was recommended) and the target activity or decision. Use a memory type that fits the fact (e.g., relationship, preference, or event). Do not skip such statements merely because they are short or embedded in a longer exchange.

solves: The diagnosed cause is that the construction agent processed a message containing explicit advice but failed to extract any candidate, so the advice was never persisted. The reusable rule is to treat explicit advice or recommendations from one speaker to another as extraction candidates regardless of the surrounding topic. This applies to any future conversation where a user offers guidance on how to do something and a downstream question may ask about that advice.
